mainEntity.name: How much does a Mitsubishi Outlander 2.4 MIVEC engine replacement cost?

acceptedAnswer.text: A used Mitsubishi Outlander 2.4 4B12 engine typically costs £400-£900, while a reconditioned unit is around £1,200-£2,200 and a fully rebuilt engine with warranty is £1,800-£3,500 [EM-QUOTE]. Used is the cheapest option but condition and history are uncertain. Reconditioned means tested and rebuilt to working standard with warranty. Rebuilt means fully stripped, inspected, rebuilt with upgraded components, 12-month warranty.

mainEntity.name: What are the signs of timing chain failure in a Mitsubishi Outlander 2.4 MIVEC?

acceptedAnswer.text: The most common early sign is a rattle on cold start lasting 1-3 seconds, caused by the chain tensioner losing hydraulic pressure. If left unchecked, chain wear can progress to cam/crank correlation faults and eventual chain jump. Valve/piston contact is catastrophic, requiring a full rebuild or replacement. The 4B12 uses a timing chain, not a belt, so there is no scheduled replacement interval, but tensioner wear is a known issue.

mainEntity.name: Is it worth replacing the engine in a Mitsubishi Outlander 2.4 MIVEC?

acceptedAnswer.text: Whether it's worth it depends on your Outlander's value, mileage, and condition. For a sub-£4,000 vehicle, a used or reconditioned engine may be more sensible than a full rebuild. For a £4,000-£8,000 vehicle, reconditioned or rebuilt with warranty is viable if keeping the car 2+ years. For a £8,000+ vehicle, replacement cost is well within vehicle value and usually the right choice.

mainEntity.name: What's the difference between the 2.4 MIVEC and the 2.2 DI-D Outlander?

acceptedAnswer.text: The 2.4 MIVEC (4B12) is a naturally aspirated petrol engine, ideal for lower-mileage, urban or family use with simpler maintenance. The 2.2 DI-D (4N14) is a turbo diesel, better for high-mileage or motorway use but with more complex emissions systems. The 4B12 petrol is generally more reliable than the 4N14 diesel, with fewer EGR/DPF complications.

mainEntity.name: Can I fit a used Outlander 2.4 MIVEC engine myself?

acceptedAnswer.text: While some DIY owners do, it is a complex job requiring engine lifting gear, specialist tools, and ECU adaptation. A used engine may need ECU reprogramming for immobiliser compatibility. Timing chain alignment must be precise, as misalignment can cause immediate damage. Many suppliers will only warranty engines fitted by a qualified garage.

mainEntity.name: How long does a Mitsubishi Outlander 2.4 MIVEC engine last?

acceptedAnswer.text: With proper maintenance - regular oil changes with the correct grade and good quality fuel - the 4B12 engine can cover 150,000-200,000 miles or more. The timing chain tensioner is the main long-term weak point. Regular oil changes (5,000-8,000 miles) reduce timing chain and piston ring wear. Correct oil spec and PCV maintenance prevent ring-sticking oil consumption.

historyTimeline.h2: Mitsubishi Outlander 2.4 MIVEC - Engine History & Specs at a Glance
historyTimeline.intro: The Mitsubishi Outlander 2.4 MIVEC, powered by the 4B12 engine, has been the core petrol offering across multiple Outlander generations. It is a naturally aspirated 2.4-litre four-cylinder from the Global Engine Alliance, used extensively in UK-market Outlanders from the second generation onward as a reliable, family-friendly SUV powertrain.

milestones.description: 4B12 MIVEC 2.4-litre petrol engine introduced in the second-generation Outlander (ZG/ZH), producing 170 hp and 226 Nm of torque, paired with a CVT or 4WD system .

Third-generation Outlander (ZK/ZL) adopts the same 4B12 engine, now rated at 167 hp with minor emissions and economy refinements; the engine remains the primary petrol option alongside the 2.2 DI-D diesel and later the PHEV .
Facelift for the third-generation Outlander, with 4B12 continuing in petrol models; subtle tuning adjustments maintain power output around 167 hp .

Fourth-generation Outlander introduces a revised 2.4-litre MIVEC engine, still designated 4B12, now used primarily in the PHEV hybrid system producing 133 hp (combined system output significantly higher) .

historyTimeline.closingNote: Every engine fitted to the Mitsubishi Outlander 2.4 MIVEC is covered below, with UK rebuilt pricing and known failure points - including the 4B12 petrol, 4N14 diesel, and PHEV hybrid powertrain for Outlander 2.4 models.

commonProblems.h2: Mitsubishi Outlander 2.4 MIVEC Engine Problems - Repair Cost vs Replacement
commonProblems.h3: The 4B12 MIVEC engine is generally a reliable, well-engineered unit - one of the better petrol engines in the Mitsubishi Outlander 2.4 MIVEC range. Most 4B12 engines cover high mileages without significant problems, provided they are serviced with the correct oil grade and interval. When failures do occur, they tend to be predictable rather than catastrophic. Rebuilt engines through EnginesMarket include upgraded components (such as improved timing chain tensioners and piston rings) addressing the original weak points, plus a minimum 12-month unlimited-mileage warranty.

problems.h4: Timing Chain Tensioner Wear - Why the Mitsubishi Outlander 2.4 MIVEC 4B12 Can Rattle on Start-Up
problems.rootCause: Timing chain tensioner wear leads to insufficient hydraulic pressure on cold start, allowing chain slack and a characteristic rattle for 1-3 seconds. The 4B12 uses a timing chain designed to last the engine's life, but tensioner deterioration can cause chain jump and valve/piston contact - catastrophic if ignored .

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replacement of chain tensioner and guides only; oil change with correct grade
repairOptions.longevity: Best for early warning rattle only; not for stretched chains

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replacement of chain, tensioner, guides, sprockets; full front-end access
repairOptions.longevity: Recommended if rattle persists or at chain service interval (if documented)

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Supply & fit rebuilt engine, upgraded components addressing the original failure point, 12-month warranty
repairOptions.longevity: When timing chain has jumped and caused internal damage

problems.vehicleValueCheck: A typical Mitsubishi Outlander 2.4 MIVEC of relevant age (2007-2015) is worth approximately £2,000-£9,000 depending on mileage and condition [THIRD-PARTY, Auto Trader/Parkers market observation]. If your vehicle is worth under £4,000, a full rebuilt engine may be financially borderline - evaluate a used engine or repair-first approach. If worth £4,000-£8,000, reconditioned or rebuilt is viable if you plan to keep the car 2+ years. If worth £8,000+, replacement cost is well within vehicle value and usually the sensible choice.
problems.recommendation: The 4B12 is a sound engine, and early intervention - replacing the chain tensioner at the first sign of cold-start rattle - is significantly cheaper than a full chain replacement or rebuild. If the chain has already jumped and bent valves, a rebuilt engine with the warranty is the safer long-term choice over a used engine of unknown history.

problems.h4: Oil Consumption & Piston Ring Sticking - What to Do About a Thirsty Outlander 2.4 MIVEC
problems.affectedModels: Mitsubishi Outlander 2.4 MIVEC (4B12, higher-mileage examples, typically 100,000+ miles)
problems.rootCause: Piston rings can become stuck with carbon deposits due to old oil, short trips, or sub-standard oil grades. This causes oil to bypass the rings and burn in the combustion chamber, leading to blue smoke, increased oil consumption, and potential catalyst damage .

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Engine flush treatment and oil change with correct oil grade
repairOptions.longevity: Best for early, mild consumption - may free stuck rings

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replacement of PCV valve and breather hoses; often overlooked but can cause ring-sticking conditions
repairOptions.longevity: Recommended if PCV system is clogged or restricted

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Engine-out rebuild, strip cylinder head, hone bores, fit new rings, check clearances
repairOptions.longevity: For significant consumption - only if vehicle value justifies the work

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Supply & fit rebuilt engine with upgraded piston rings, 12-month warranty
repairOptions.longevity: If consumption is high and vehicle worth £5,000+

problems.vehicleValueCheck: Apply the same value framework as above. For a typical Outlander 2.4 MIVEC, a piston ring replacement may cost 60-100% of the vehicle's value. If you're burning more than 1 litre of oil per 1,000 miles and the car is worth under £4,000, consider a used engine or scrapping. If worth £5,000+, a rebuilt engine with warranty offers long-term peace of mind.
problems.recommendation: Before committing to a rebuild, try the low-cost options first - a good engine flush, PCV valve replacement, and fresh high-quality oil of the correct grade can sometimes free sticking rings. If consumption persists, weigh the replacement cost against the vehicle value and your ownership horizon.
problems.cta: -> Compare rebuilt 4B12 Mitsubishi Outlander 2.4 MIVEC engine prices

problems.h4: Cold-Start Stalling & Idle Issues - Is Your Outlander 2.4 MIVEC Struggling to Start?
problems.rootCause: Multiple owner reports suggest the 4B12 can suffer from cold-start stalling, where the engine starts, revs briefly to around 1,500 rpm, then drops to 700 rpm and stalls. Common fixes include throttle body cleaning, fuel filter replacement, and PCV valve replacement .

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Remove throttle body, clean carbon deposits, reset ECU adaptation
repairOptions.longevity: First step for idle issues and stalling

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replace in-tank fuel filter (strainer) or complete fuel pump module
repairOptions.longevity: If filter clogged - common cause of first-start stalling

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replace PCV valve - can cause idle issues and oil consumption
repairOptions.longevity: Often overlooked but reported to resolve stalling

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: ECU reset and throttle learn procedure - free to do yourself
repairOptions.longevity: Sometimes resolves idle issues without parts

problems.vehicleValueCheck: These repairs are relatively inexpensive and well within the value of any Outlander 2.4 MIVEC. Consider them preventative maintenance rather than a replacement trigger.
problems.recommendation: Start with the cheapest fix - many owners report success with throttle body cleaning and adaptation reset. If the issue persists, change the fuel filter (the in-tank strainer can clog with age) and inspect the PCV system. These are minor repairs that should not trigger a replacement decision.
